preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10^5) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(n == int(n) and 1 <= n <= 10**5 for n in (line.split()[0] for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2]))
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first line is an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5) representing the length of the permutation.

preconditions.expression: all(len(a) == n and all(int(x) == x and 1 <= x <= n for x in a) and len(set(a)) == n for a, n in zip((line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::2]), (int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2])))
preconditions.description: For each test case, the second line contains n distinct integers a_i (1 ≤ a_i ≤ n) representing a permutation of length n.
The sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 10^5.

postconditions.expression: all(len(stdout_lines) == 1 + k for k, stdout_lines in zip((int(stdout.splitlines()[i]) for i in range(0, len(stdout.splitlines()), k+1)), [stdout.splitlines()[i+1:i+1+k] for i, k in enumerate((int(stdout.splitlines()[i]) for i in range(0, len(stdout.splitlines()), k+1)))]))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output consists of k+1 lines: the first line is k (1 ≤ k ≤ f(n)), followed by k lines describing subsequences, where each subsequence line starts with its length l_i (1 ≤ l_i ≤ n) followed by l_i integers.

postconditions.expression: all(all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in line.split()[1:]) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: Each subsequence contains integers from the original permutation, each between 1 and n.

postconditions.expression: all(len(set(line.split()[1:])) == len(line.split()[1:]) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: Each subsequence contains distinct integers (no duplicates).

postconditions.expression: all(all(a[i] in line.split()[1:] for i, a in enumerate(permutation)) for permutation, line in zip(([int(x) for x in stdin.splitlines()[i+1]] for i in range(0, len(stdin.splitlines()), 2)), stdout.splitlines()[1:]))
postconditions.description: Every element of the permutation appears in exactly one subsequence.

postconditions.expression: all(all((line.split()[1:][i] < line.split()[1:][i+1] for i in range(len(line.split()[1:])-1)) or all(line.split()[1:][i] > line.split()[1:][i+1] for i in range(len(line.split()[1:])-1))) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: Each subsequence is either strictly increasing or strictly decreasing.

postconditions.expression: all(len(set.union(*(set(line.split()[1:]) for line in stdout.splitlines()[i+1:i+1+k]))) == n for i, k in enumerate((int(stdout.splitlines()[i]) for i in range(0, len(stdout.splitlines()), k+1))))
postconditions.description: The union of all subsequences for a test case contains all elements of the permutation exactly once.

postconditions.expression: all(k <= f(n) for k, n in zip((int(stdout.splitlines()[i]) for i in range(0, len(stdout.splitlines()), k+1)), (int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2])))
postconditions.description: The number of subsequences k for each test case is at most f(n), where f(n) is the minimum integer such that every permutation of length n can be partitioned into at most k monotonic subsequences.
